content.text: The backend with which we are concerned is
. This backend does require an LDCache implementation behind it. I think a simple in-memory implementation wrapping a Guava Cache is a good way to start.

Unfortunately, Marmotta technology relies on very old versions of Commons HTTP and Sesame. The HTTP client dependencies, in particular, are blocked by Maven Enforcer's com.redhat.victims rules. Closing in favor of another approach.

I'd like to replace the jena backend for fcrepo-transform in order to migrate to jena 3.x. I could write a shim to convert the jena model to a sesame graph (and use the sesame backend), but the linkeddata backend is, as described above, significantly more powerful. If I relax the maven enforcer for just the transform module, it is possible to use the linkeddata backend. Thoughts?
Are you going to use an in-memory only approach for this, or something that persists to disk?

At present, I'm using spring injection with the fallback being filesystem-based persistence. Once the MODE5 branch is merged, the infinispan (in memory) option may be a good option, but at present that's not possible b/c of dependency conflicts (marmotta:ldcache-backend-infinispan uses ISPN 6.x and MODE4 uses ISPN 7.x)
If we do an in-memory version (which I think would actually make a better default) how about a simple single-node-assumption impl of LDCache using something like Guava's Cache API?

I agree that an in-memory impl using Guava's cache API makes a lot of sense. At present, I need to rework quite a bit of the fcrepo-transform code in order to pass in a shared cache to each request. There's also some complexity related to AuthN. And so at this point, I'd like to use an existing impl of Marmotta's LDCachingBackend rather than creating our own implementation of their LDCachingBackend API (just to simplify the extent of this change).
I would imagine the cache being injected, like the XServices, and I suspect that actually, doing a Guava impl of LDCache might be
than bringing in something as weighty as a new ISPN instance. But I leave it to you to explore.
I have to add that this feature rocks!

There are a few minor code review comments, but the most pressing issue is that the basic, default /fcr:transform capability does not appear to work.
Hopefully I am missing something simple in my testing approach.
I am going to pursue a completely different tack here. Instead, I propose reimplementing this as a camel/karaf-based service and completely deprecating the fcrepo-transform module.

Currently, Fedora uses: ldpath-backend-jena, https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-transform/blob/master/pom.xml#L106-L114
Available backends: https://marmotta.apache.org/ldpath/index.html#Backend_Modules

The backend with which we are concerned is ldpath-backend-linkeddata. This backend does require an LDCache implementation behind it. I think a simple in-memory implementation wrapping a Guava Cache is a good way to start.

Unfortunately, Marmotta technology relies on very old versions of Commons HTTP and Sesame. The HTTP client dependencies, in particular, are blocked by Maven Enforcer's com.redhat.victims rules. Closing in favor of another approach.

If I relax the maven enforcer for just the transform module, it is possible to use the linkeddata backend. Thoughts?

fcrepo-webapp-plus: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/43

I agree that an in-memory impl using Guava's cache API makes a lot of sense. At present, I need to rework quite a bit of the fcrepo-transform code in order to pass in a shared cache to each request. There's also some complexity related to AuthN. And so at this point, I'd like to use an existing impl of Marmotta's LDCachingBackend rather than creating our own implementation of their LDCachingBackend API (just to simplify the extent of this change).

PRs:
fcrepo-transform:https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-transform/pull/26
fcrepo-webapp-plus: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/44

I have to add that this feature rocks!

After creating a resource at the top-level of the repository(`/rest/test`), the default transform appears to no longer returning a meaningful result:

curl -uadmin1:password3  localhost:8080/rest/test/fcr:transform/default

There are a few minor code review comments, but the most pressing issue is that the basic, default /fcr:transform capability does not appear to work.
Hopefully I am missing something simple in my testing approach.

I am going to pursue a completely different tack here. Instead, I propose reimplementing this as a camel/karaf-based service and completely deprecating the fcrepo-transform module.

At present, I have an implementation of fcrepo-ldpath that will be made part of fcrepo-camel-toolbox. I have unit and integration tests in place and am verifying karaf-based deployment.

Andrew Woods do you have any concerns about this approach? If not, I will close the current PRs referenced here and work toward deprecating fcrepo-transform.
As a point of information, Unknown's new tack was discussed at today's tech call and met with uniform approval.

Unknown, since the primary usage of fcrepo-transform has been in the context of indexing Solr, which we offer through Camel and since the Transform capability maps well into the API-X pattern, at a general level this move seems reasonable.
Do you plan on working this into the API-X framework?
Can you describe your proposed interaction model?
PR: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/pull/103

Andrew Woods The interaction model is almost identical to the existing fcr:transform feature. For a resource at, say, http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/resource/path, you would interact with the service like so:

curl -XGET http://localhost:4444/ldpath/resource/path?ldpath=http://example.org/myldpath

OR

curl -XPOST http://localhost:4444/ldpath/resource/path -d @myldpath.txt -H"Content-Type: text/plain"

OR (for the default transform)

curl -XGET http://localhost:4444/ldpath/resource/path

There is no facility for storing ldpath programs such as there is with fcr-transform, but if that is truly desired it would be easy to add.
Unknown, are you anticipating a follow-on task of adding a test to: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-tests ?
Pending response to some minor code review comments... otherwise this looks and works great.
Code review comments have been addressed in a new commit to this PR.
Andrew Woods yes, you can expect a follow-on PR for fcrepo-camel-tests that will include tests for the fcrepo-ldpath module.
Resolved with: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/commit/3a6cc7f6b1ca56d75e0248a3e9a72f81f2319cb3
